sampling_model.design: A triangular array of binary sequential experiments with fixed finite-population potential outcomes and assignment as the only randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: Given \(\mathcal F_{n,t-1}\), \(A_{nt}\) is Bernoulli with known logged predictable probability \(e_{nt}\).
sampling_model.overlap: The rare-arm probability follows \(t e_{nt}\approx \bar q(t/n)\) after an early cutoff, with bounded cumulative hazard and \(0<e_{nt}\le\rho<1\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Predictable regressions \(m_{nt}(a)\) may be arbitrary within their bound; their treated residuals follow a deterministic Lipschitz profile on one common high-probability event.
sampling_model.randomness: Only the known adaptive randomization law is random; there is no superpopulation sampling assumption.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Definition 1 permits general positive history-dependent assignment probabilities, while Theorem 4(ii)'s Gaussian AIPW conclusion requires Condition 3, including its negligible-maximum part (ii).
Theorem 1 constructs doubly robust betting confidence sequences under predictable logging.
Proposition 1 proves selective type-I error control for the selective randomization p-value.
Theorem 1 proves asymptotic type-I error control for simulation with optimism in specified adaptive designs.
Proposition 2 gives an exact compound-Poisson law for an HT rate estimator under independent Poisson importance sampling.
Finite-population limited-overlap estimators are asymptotically Gaussian when their effective sample size diverges.
Any valid i.i.d. bounded-mean confidence interval obeys an inverse-information-projection width lower bound.
Stein perturbation yields explicit total-variation compound-Poisson approximation bounds for integer-valued sums.
Weighted Bernoulli and Poisson sums admit generalized Dickman approximation bounds.
Theorem 1 gives a semiparametrically efficient Gaussian limit for the truncated A2IPW estimator.
Resampling simulations find tighter superior-arm and wider inferior-arm intervals under real-time adaptive randomization.

body.tldr: At the critical rare-arm boundary, the finite-population AIPW error need not be Gaussian. On this note's original structured binary profile subclass, a stopped adaptive-to-Bernoulli-to-Poisson transfer and directed-rational convolution give a computable atom-safe interval with uniform randomization coverage and explicit oracle slack. Separately, the retained constant-intensity clipped-ramp theorem optimizes the residual late-void obstruction under structured-class honesty. A distinct pointwise-minimal intensity \(q_\star(u)=\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\}\) yields the jointly optimized pair-honesty envelope \(\left[\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha\right]_+\), with residual and intensity elbows that may occur in either order. Direct every-\(n\) inclusion transfers only this converse to Li and Zhao's baseline adaptive class. Exact attainment is pairwise only. The exact \(1/8\), \(0.60710678\), directed \(13/32\), and high-hazard \(0.442M\) results remain unchanged.

project_justification.gap: Li and Zhao's baseline adaptive-design class permits positive history-dependent assignment probabilities, but their Gaussian AIPW theorem requires a negligible-maximum condition that fails at bounded cumulative hazard. Existing adaptive and i.i.d. width results neither calibrate the signed atomic compound-Poisson law nor jointly optimize the complete-log common-void obstruction over the declared intensity, outcome-bound, and residual-Lipschitz restrictions.
project_justification.niche: The boundary has distinct positive and converse deliverables. Structured deterministic profiles support computable atom-safe calibration. For information limits, the retained constant-intensity clipped ramp optimizes residual separation, while the separate profile \(q_\star(u)=\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\}\) is pointwise minimal in \(\mathcal Q\) and therefore maximizes late-void mass for each fixed start. Combining the two yields a pair-honesty frontier with both intensity and residual elbows.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies the finite adaptive-to-Poisson transfer and profile-net interval theorem on the original structured subclass, the retained exact constant-intensity clipped-ramp tradeoff, and a separate exact intensity-optimized two-sign tradeoff. The new joint envelope is proved under honesty for the selected pair because the new family's profile event is guaranteed only eventually, not for every \(n\). A direct baseline-class inclusion argument transfers only the converse to Li and Zhao's class; pairwise attainment and positive calibration retain their separate scopes.

body.related_work: Li and Zhao (2026) provide the closest design-based setup: fixed finite-population potential outcomes, positive assignment probabilities that may be prespecified functions of history, and predictable AIPW regression. Their baseline binary class contains both the retained constant-intensity clipped ramps and the separate intensity-optimized arrays for every \(n\), but their Theorem 4(ii) assumes Condition 3; both bounded-hazard witnesses fail its negligible-maximum part because late standardized increments remain nonnegligible. The constant-intensity structured-class converse and the direct baseline-class joint-intensity converse are therefore logically separate. Only converse bounds transfer; matching confidence-set constructions remain sharp inside selected two-sign experiments, and the positive profile-net theorem remains confined to this note's original structured subclass. Bibaut and Kallus (2025) organize adaptive inference into Gaussian repair, always-valid methods, and direct inversion of nonnormal laws. Waudby-Smith et al. (2024), Freidling, Zhao, and Gao (2026), and Cho, Bibaut, and Kallus (2025) do not supply the present finite-population signed atomic calibration or jointly optimized common-void envelope. Chen et al. (2026) obtain a compound-Poisson HT law under independent Poisson importance sampling, while Hong, Leung, and Li (2020) treat limited overlap with diverging effective information. Shekhar and Ramdas (2023) prove i.i.d. bounded-mean width bounds. Barbour and Xia (1999) support compound-Poisson error accounting, and Bhattacharjee and Goldstein (2019) identify the generalized Dickman constant-profile reduction. Liberali et al. (2025) remain the applied consumer, conditional on a prespecified expected-endpoint bridge for GUSTO-1 and EUROPA.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The finite-transfer theorem couples the AIPW statistic, not the complete experiments, and therefore does not imply the all-estimator lower bounds. Those bounds instead use exact common subprobabilities on late-arm void events. The retained constant-intensity theorem has its original structured-class premise. For the separate intensity-optimized family, \(G_n=\Omega\) is proved only eventually: at a finite included index where \(q_\star(t/n)/t>\rho\), the intensity discrepancy can exceed \(\delta_{q,n}\). Its joint frontier therefore assumes honesty on the selected pair rather than all-\(n\) membership in the structured class. Both matching procedures know their selected pair, so neither establishes global minimax attainment. Li--Zhao inclusion transfers only converse bounds. The positive theorem still requires its supplied profile and early-variation contracts, and the \(0.442M\) high-hazard result remains a subfamily upper bound. The polynomial bit-complexity question remains open because no polynomial bound controls profile boxes straddling the certification boundary.
body.honest_scope: Uniform finite-experiment coverage applies to the original bounded Lipschitz intensity and signed-residual profile subclass with its supplied common profile event, early quadratic-variation envelope, and certified inputs. The constant-intensity envelope \([(1-x(d))^c-2\alpha]_+\) retains its structured-class honesty premise. The stronger joint-intensity envelope \(\left[\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha\right]_+\) is a pair-honesty conclusion for the separate \(q_\star\) experiment, whose profile contract is only eventually exact. Direct every-\(n\) baseline inclusion transfers that joint converse, but neither positive calibration nor attainment, to Li and Zhao's class. Exact attainment is confined to each selected two-sign pair; no global minimax procedure is claimed. The original linear-ramp frontier, exact \(1/8\) and \(0.60710678\) diagnostic with its \(\rho\ge1/2\) cap qualification, directed \(13/32\) certificate, and high-hazard \(0.442M\) radius remain valid. No polynomial certificate-complexity exponent is asserted. The Liberali et al. application remains conditional on a prespecified expected-endpoint bridge.
